messages:
Maya Li: FYI acct_acme_001 reported a dashboard vs invoice mismatch. Invoice total is $1,243.21 higher than the dashboard for Mar 2025. Customer called out the usage line 'usage-embedding' — invoice tokens = 1,217,304, dashboard tokens = 1,204,987. Can someone look?

Casey (Support): Account ID and invoice/export available? I'll pull the invoice lines.

Maya Li: acct_acme_001. Query I ran: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM usage WHERE account='acct_acme_001' AND ts >= '2025-03-01' AND ts < '2025-04-01'; returned 1204987.

Oliver Park: I can confirm invoice export: invoice.tokens = 1217304. That's +12,317 tokens vs your dashboard. Possible backfill or window mismatch.

Sarah Kim (CS): :eyes: Customer denies any bulk import on their side. Could be our ingestion/backfill.

BillingBot: Invoice export created: /exports/invoice_acct_acme_2025-03.csv (sha256: abc123def456...). Billing job completed at 2025-04-01T07:05:02Z.

Casey (Support): Quick thought — dashboard uses UTC day boundaries, billing historically used account TZ for cutoff. What's acct_acme_001 timezone?

Maya Li: Account timezone is stored as America/Los_Angeles. My dashboard query used UTC window.

Oliver Park: That would shift the cutoff by 7/8 hours (depending on DST). Re-run aggregate using account TZ — could explain ~12k tokens if many requests happened around the boundary.

Oliver Park: ```
-- repro: aggregate in account TZ
SELECT sum(tokens) AS tokens_pst
FROM usage
WHERE account='acct_acme_001'
  AND ts >= CONVERT_TZ('2025-03-01 00:00:00','America/Los_Angeles','UTC')
  AND ts <  CONVERT_TZ('2025-04-01 00:00:00','America/Los_Angeles','UTC');
```

BillingBot: Billing pipeline note: final aggregation window applied customer TZ cutoff for invoice generation. Backfill jobs (if any) were run between 2025-04-01T06:30Z and 2025-04-01T07:10Z.

Oliver Park: Ran the account-TZ query — result: 1,217,310 tokens. That narrows the gap: invoice 1,217,304 vs account-TZ aggregate 1,217,310 = -6 tokens. Dashboard-UTC was 1,204,987. So ~12.3k of the delta is explained by timezone/window. Remaining difference is tiny (6 tokens).

Casey (Support): 6 tokens is trivial but still need root cause. Could be rounding, micro-batching, or a duplicate/late replay. Check adjustments/credits table and ingestion logs around 2025-03-31T23:59:xx PST.

Maya Li: I checked credits and adjustments for acct_acme_001 for March — none. However there was a small spike of many sub-100-token requests at 2025-03-31T23:59:56 PST coming from embedder-service.

Sarah Kim (CS): Next steps proposal: (1) eng run a dedupe check for requests in that second (2) billing reconcile the invoice/export to the raw event stream (3) reply to customer with ETA and provisional guidance.

Oliver Park: I ran an event dedupe diff against ingestion logs: found 6 near-identical requests with distinct request_ids but identical payloads that were ingested due to a retry that missed an idempotency key when the embedder retried on a 502. That explains the +6.

Casey (Support): Good catch. So final breakdown: ~12,317 explained by timezone/window shift, +6 explained by duplicate retry.

BillingBot: Billing ops: issue a 6-token credit for acct_acme_001. Credit amount = $0.06 USD (per-token unit price).

Maya Li: I'll send the customer an update: summary, root causes, and confirm the 6-token credit. Draft: "We found two causes — boundary/window mismatch between dashboard (UTC) and invoice (account TZ) which explains the majority of the delta, plus 6 duplicated tokens from a transient retry in the embedder pipeline; we will credit the 6 tokens. We're adding a guard to ensure retries include idempotency keys."

Sarah Kim (CS): Perfect. Can eng add a small regression check for end-of-day spikes around cutoffs so we catch large boundary-sensitive deltas earlier?

Oliver Park: Will add a one-off monitor for cutoff deltas and a fix to the embedder retry idempotency. I’ll post a PR link when ready.

Casey (Support): I'll update the case notes and close after customer ack. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
